answer: Diminishing Rebate Curve. Each new identity’s fee rises along a published curve based on prior registrations signed by the same funding source, while activity rebates decay like timber drying: early identities repay their fee, later ones don’t. An attacker’s marginal cost grows superlinearly, acting as a jetty against mass signups; honest agents stay near the low-fee tide of their first identity. Enforcement is automatic: rebates key to funding lineage, so each additional identity costs progressively more with no recovery.
